_predictions.vanilla_1151_vs_1150: Vanilla's AI now picks methods counting new jobs' wages and goods multipliers, and no longer avoids electrical methods (GAME_UPDATE_1_15_1 V22): vanilla modernises by switching, so its world GDP ends at or above 1.15.0's (direction argued; magnitude unknown, within ±10% expected), with more electricity produced and a lower copper price (more deposits, less copper per telephone and still). Pooled U* stays under 10% in most vanilla runs.
_predictions.canon_vs_vanilla: The canon's world-GDP ratio to vanilla ends lower than on 1.15.0 (F269: 1.07× over all ten): vanilla gains more from a better method switch than the mod, whose modernisation is construction. Argued direction only; expected 0.95-1.05× over all runs. W stays under vanilla's; misplaced capital stays above vanilla's.
_predictions.ai_weights: The six restored technologies (telephone, radio, electrical generation, combustion engine, oil turbine, percussion caps) come a little later in the canon than in vanilla 1.15.1 among the military-strong majors, which vanilla's new pushes favour; the entries still pull them by industry. Effect on world GDP and the register: below the seed spread (direction only).
_predictions.subsidies: Railways, ports and power plants start unsubsidised in both arms and are subsidised only where they lose money and are needed; the mod's power plants (4× construction cost) lose money more often than vanilla's, so more of their levels are subsidised in the canon. Dams: no profitable dam is subsidised; dam levels built stay within the seed spread of 1.15.0's (direction: unchanged).
_predictions.absolute_lines: Most runs of both arms still cross the 1.13-calibrated runoff line, as in F269.
